subject: chemistry
topicDisplay: Reactivity series and extraction of metals
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Eduqas spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Eduqas Chemistry simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: reactions of metals with water and acid
reduction of metal oxides with carbon
extraction of iron in the blast furnace
the OIL RIG rule and half equations

questions.q: Which of these metals is the most reactive?
questions.explain: Potassium is high in the reactivity series (very reactive). Gold and copper are unreactive; iron is moderately reactive.

questions.q: Carbon and hydrogen are included in the reactivity series because:
options: Their position decides which extraction method is used
questions.explain: Placing carbon (and hydrogen) in the series shows which metals can be extracted by reduction with carbon and which need electrolysis.

questions.lo: reactions of metals with water and acid
questions.q: When a reactive metal reacts with dilute acid, the gas produced is:
questions.explain: Metal + acid -> salt + hydrogen. The hydrogen gas produced gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint.

questions.lo: reactions of metals with water and acid
questions.q: Which metal reacts most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explain: Sodium (Group 1) reacts vigorously with cold water. Magnesium reacts only very slowly with cold water; zinc and iron barely react.

questions.q: What happens when an iron nail is placed in copper sulfate solution?
options: Iron displaces copper; the nail becomes coated in copper
questions.explain: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper: Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu. The blue solution fades and copper coats the nail.

questions.q: Which pair would give NO displacement reaction?
questions.explain: A less reactive metal cannot displace a more reactive one. Copper is below zinc, so copper cannot displace zinc from zinc sulfate.

questions.q: In terms of oxygen, reduction is defined as:
questions.explain: In terms of oxygen, reduction is loss of oxygen and oxidation is gain of oxygen. (In terms of electrons, reduction is gain of electrons.)

questions.q: In the reaction 2CuO + C -> 2Cu + CO2, the carbon is:
questions.explain: Carbon gains oxygen (to form CO2), so it is oxidised. The copper oxide loses oxygen, so it is reduced.

questions.q: Metals more reactive than carbon are usually extracted by:
questions.explain: Metals above carbon in the reactivity series (e.g. aluminium) are too reactive to be reduced by carbon and must be extracted by electrolysis.

questions.q: Why can gold be found in the Earth as the pure metal (native)?
options: It is so unreactive it does not readily form compounds
questions.explain: Gold is so unreactive that it exists uncombined (as the element) in nature, so it does not need to be extracted from a compound.

questions.lo: reduction of metal oxides with carbon
questions.q: Which metal can be extracted by reduction with carbon?
questions.explain: Zinc is below carbon in the reactivity series, so it can be extracted by reduction with carbon. Aluminium, calcium and sodium are above carbon and need electrolysis.

questions.lo: reduction of metal oxides with carbon
questions.q: In carbon reduction, the carbon acts as:
questions.explain: Carbon removes oxygen from the metal oxide, so it is the reducing agent (it is itself oxidised).

questions.lo: extraction of iron in the blast furnace
questions.q: In the blast furnace, which substance mainly reduces iron(III) oxide to iron?
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is the main reducing agent: Fe2O3 + 3CO -> 2Fe + 3CO2. Coke burns to make CO2, which then reacts with more coke to form CO.

questions.lo: extraction of iron in the blast furnace
questions.q: What is limestone (calcium carbonate) added to the blast furnace to do?
questions.explain: Limestone decomposes to calcium oxide, which reacts with sandy (acidic) impurities to form slag, removing them from the iron.

questions.q: During electrolysis, positive metal ions move to the:
questions.explain: Positive ions (cations) are attracted to the negative electrode (cathode), where metals are deposited.

questions.q: Why is cryolite added to the aluminium oxide during aluminium extraction?
options: To lower the melting point, saving energy
questions.explain: Aluminium oxide has a very high melting point. Dissolving it in molten cryolite lowers the operating temperature, reducing energy use and cost.

questions.q: Why must the carbon anodes in aluminium extraction be replaced regularly?
options: Oxygen produced reacts with them, burning them away
questions.explain: Oxygen forms at the positive carbon anode and reacts with it to form CO2, so the anodes gradually burn away and must be replaced.

questions.lo: the OIL RIG rule and half equations
questions.q: At the cathode: Al3+ + 3e- -> Al. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Gaining electrons is reduction (OIL RIG: Reduction Is Gain of electrons). Al3+ gains 3 electrons to form aluminium metal at the cathode.

questions.lo: the OIL RIG rule and half equations
questions.q: At the anode during electrolysis of molten aluminium oxide, oxide ions form oxygen. This is:
questions.explain: 2O2- -> O2 + 4e-. Losing electrons is oxidation (OIL: Oxidation Is Loss of electrons), which occurs at the positive anode.

questions.q: Which is a key advantage of recycling metals rather than extracting new metal?
options: It removes the need for any energy
It uses less energy and conserves limited ore reserves
questions.explain: Recycling uses much less energy than extraction from ore, conserves finite ore reserves and reduces waste sent to landfill.
